purpose: Check whether primary or otherwise reviewable sources provide fish survey results tied to the eight newly named Guinayangan freshwater leads. This records a bounded search, not evidence that fish are absent.
queries: Guinayangan Quezon freshwater fish survey Maulawin spring fish species
site:denr.gov.ph Guinayangan fish species river survey Quezon
site:bmb.gov.ph "Maulawin Spring" fish fauna OR fish species
site:repository.seafdec.org Guinayangan Quezon fish survey river

sourcesReviewed.result: Official 2024 article describes a municipality-level reconnaissance, local aquaculture-farm visits, tilapia-fingerling distribution to smallholders, a possible Fish Conservation Zone in Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape, and seven unnamed lagoons. It provides no fish taxa survey, sampling stations, lagoon identities, or record explicitly tied to any target lead.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Context/discovery only. Fingerling distribution is not natural wild occurrence; no species assigned to the river, springs, protected landscape, or De Guzman Fishpond.

sourcesReviewed.result: Official BMB Protected Area Information System page appeared in search results. The indexed excerpt lists broad biological-feature sections; direct page retrieval returned HTTP 502, so the detailed profile could not be inspected.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Discovery lead only. No species row, absence claim, geometry, or site crosswalk was extracted.

sourcesReviewed.result: Annex J confirms the source-named river and seven spring-source entries and their barangay-level water-supply context; it contains no fish survey.
PSA PSGC confirms the administrative barangay names/codes only.

Corrected CoL XR Actinopterygii filter: 8 target waterBody names, 8 exact target locality strings, and locality variants Hinabaan, Maulawin, and Guinayangan returned zero. A broader all-taxa Guinayangan locality search returned 129 mixed records; it was not used to assign fish to any target waterbody. A separate follow-up screen for the four IIRR-named tributaries is recorded in calabarzon-guinayangan-tributary-gbif-screen-20261030.json; all eight supplied-name queries returned zero, which is not fish-absence evidence.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Bounded GBIF search gap only. No occurrence row, fish species, geometry, locality assignment, or absence claim added.

sourcesReviewed.result: Official CLSU FAC page lists fac@clsu.edu.ph.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Used only as the published destination for an unsent data-access inquiry.

sourcesReviewed.result: DENR CALABARZON directory search excerpt lists CENRO Calauag office location and telephone; direct page open returned HTTP 403 and no current email was visible.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Used only as a routing lead; draft says verify contact information before any call or request.

sourcesReviewed.result: The IIRR watershed brief names four Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape tributaries and provides approximate/historical watershed context for Hiwasayan River. The reviewed pages contain no fish survey, fish taxa, sampling stations, or current occurrence data.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Watershed-name discovery context only. Do not treat as fish evidence, current presence, a complete inventory, surveyed route, geometry, salinity, or fishing permission.

limitations: Search-engine results are discovery aids, not a complete search of all theses, protected-area records, and unpublished monitoring data.
The BMB PAIS page could not be directly reviewed after an HTTP 502 response; do not infer what its full record contains.
The CLSU article concerns local aquaculture activity but does not publish a fish inventory or identify its seven visited lagoons.
The Tayabas River study is not a source for the Hinabaan River or Guinayangan springs.
The initial GBIF default-backbone key attempt was invalidated because the retrieved usage key was deleted; only the corrected CoL XR key/checklist search is reported as fish-filtered evidence.
nextAction: Seek a permitted copy or station-level species list from the Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape PAMO/BMB and the CLSU-IIRR Guinayangan aquaculture research team. In parallel, use GBIF exact text queries only as candidate discovery; require explicit occurrence locality and identity, date, method, taxonomic rank, and record-level terms before any fish assertion.

taxonomy.label: Catalogue of Life Extended Release Actinopterygii; same corrected CoL XR filter used in existing project research.

broaderAllTaxaQuery.decision: Not used as fish evidence: all-taxon locality results are mixed and at least one returned sample had stateProvince=Rizal despite locality=Guinayangan. No individual occurrence was admitted.

invalidatedPreliminaryAttempt.note: An earlier default-backbone taxon filter was not used: GBIF /species/204 reports that usage as deleted 2022-11-23. The fish-filtered screen above instead used the existing project CoL XR checklist/taxon pair.
invalidatedPreliminaryAttempt.queryEvidence: The default /species/match?name=Actinopterygii returned matchType NONE; no result from that attempt is interpreted.

gbifOccurrenceScreen.interpretation: All query counts are bounded indexed-text screens. Zero text matches are not evidence that fish are absent and do not replace a field survey or complete occurrence download.

requestDraft.handling: Draft routes the CLSU data inquiry to its published FAC contact and proposes that CENRO Calauag supply the current PAMO request channel; verify the CENRO phone and do not infer data access or permission.
